Wharton Alum Champions League
Official Keeper Rules
- Auction draft format
- Starting in 2016, each team will be allowed to retain 4 Keepers from their roster at the end of the last season (increased from 3 keepers in 2015)
- 4 keeper spots per team
- Keeper selection deadline is indicated on the Yahoo league website (~2 days before Draft day)

- Starting in 2018, the max contract for keepers will be 4 years (i.e. you can keep a player for 3 additional seasons following the year in which you draft such player, regardless of when he was drafted)
- You do not have to keep a player for the max contract
- If a contracted player is dropped and then picked up as free agent or waiver, then the contract year still applies for keeper purposes (i.e. contract does not reset)
- Any player that is dropped back into the draft pool, and not picked up, is free game to be drafted at the then market Cost in subsequent drafts
- Cost of each keeper is their draft value from the prior season (even if they were dropped during the season and then picked up as free agent), subject to FAAB rules below
- Cost of undrafted free agent keepers picked up during the season will be $5
- The total cost of your keepers will be deducted from your starting dollars available for the draft
- NO RENTAL TRADES!
- Kickers removed starting in 2020
- New FAAB Budget for Waivers:
$100 FAAB per team per season - tiebreaker is the reverse weekly standings
Keeper Cost of waiver pickups will be based on a sliding scale determined by % of FAAB spent (0-20% = $5; 21-40% = $10; 41-60% = $15; >60% = $20)

If a player is picked up and dropped through waivers multiple times during the season, the keeper cost will be based on the last waiver bid process of the season that resulted in the player being added to the ending roster.

If a player is drafted in the auction, and then subsequently dropped and picked up off waivers, then the keeper cost will be the GREATER OF: 1) the auction draft value, or 2) the cost determined by the last waiver bid process
Anti-Dumping Rule: *
- Applies to trades within 1 week of trade deadline or as applied by the Commissioner at his discretion
- Trade deadline will be set on the Yahoo Fantasy League Page (see "Settings")
- If any trade involves less than $10 of cash transfer in the subsequent year, then the commissioner may hold the trade for 24 hours in order to do a "Market Check"
(For example, a $5/$10 trade will automatically trigger a market check, but a $10/$2 trade will not).
- The $10 trigger is a level I chose based on where trading activity has occurred historically and based on my view of what is a meaningful amount of draft dollars
- Any manager will have the next 24 hours to offer the Seller a better trade proposal for that player.
- Once the 24 hour market check is complete, Seller shall give the manager that originally accepted the trade a "Right of First Refusal" on any proposal that comes in during the "Market Check"
- Then Seller can proceed with executing the trade either with the original manager (in a case where ROFR was exercised) or with any other manager (if ROFR not exercised)
* Note: Anti-Dumping rule may be imposed at Commish's discretion throughout the season and off-season.
This rule is meant to minimize the Commish veto and allow efficient markets to dictate trade activity.
